2608.10319.title: Do Personalized Skills Help Coding Agents? An Empirical Study of Developer Interaction Histories
2608.10319.paper_summary: Large language model (LLM)-powered agents have rapidly evolved from code-completion tools into solvers of complex software engineering tasks. As developers collaborate with coding agents over time, their preferences emerge through repeated interactions and can be used to adapt agent behavior to better meet individual developers' needs. Capturing and reusing these preferences may reduce repeated corrections and improve developer-agent collaboration. Agent skills provide a lightweight mechanism for transferring experience without modifying model parameters. However, existing work primarily focuses on task-specific skills, and it remains unclear whether developer-specific skills distilled from interaction histories can generalize to future tasks. We propose a framework for extracting reusable developer preferences from interaction traces. It first generates personalized skills through rule-based bootstrapping and evidence-grounded refinement, and then evaluates them using a reproducible replay framework with an interactive, trajectory-conditioned LLM-based human developer simulator. We conduct an experiment on 206 real-world developer-agent sessions from 13 developers and compare personalized skills against no-skill, generic-skill, and other-user-skill baselines. Personalized skills provide small and inconsistent improvements over the no-skill baseline, whereas generic skills pooled across developers achieve the largest and most consistent gains. Further analysis suggests that personalized skills become more effective when developer preferences appear frequently, particularly when their histories contain multiple examples relevant to future tasks. These findings provide empirical insights into when developer-specific personalization is effective and demonstrate that broadly transferable procedural knowledge can be more robust than developer-specific preference signals.
2608.10319.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型 (LLM) 驅動的代理迅速從代碼補全工具演變為解決複雜軟體工程任務的工具。隨著開發者隨著時間與編碼代理合作，他們的偏好通過反覆互動而浮現，並可以用來調整代理行為，以更好地滿足個別開發者的需求。捕捉和重用這些偏好可以減少重複修正並改善開發者與代理的合作。代理技能提供了一種輕量級的機制，用於在不修改模型參數的情況下轉移經驗。然而，現有的研究主要集中在特定任務的技能上，尚不清楚從互動歷史中提煉出的開發者特定技能是否能夠泛化到未來的任務。我們提出了一個從互動痕跡中提取可重用開發者偏好的框架。它首先通過基於規則的自舉和基於證據的精煉生成個性化技能，然後使用可重現的重播框架進行評估，該框架包含一個互動的、基於軌跡的 LLM 驅動的人類開發者模擬器。我們對來自 13 位開發者的 206 個真實開發者-代理會話進行了實驗，並將個性化技能與無技能、通用技能和其他用戶技能基準進行比較。個性化技能相對於無技能基準提供了小而不一致的改進，而跨開發者的通用技能則實現了最大的和最一致的增益。進一步分析表明，當開發者的偏好頻繁出現時，個性化技能變得更加有效，特別是當他們的歷史包含多個與未來任務相關的例子時。這些發現為開發者特定個性化何時有效提供了實證見解，並表明廣泛可轉移的程序性知識可能比開發者特定的偏好信號更具穩健性。
